questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a container and a virtual machine?

options.text: A container includes its own full operating system, a VM does not
A container shares the host's kernel and is an isolated process; a VM runs its own guest OS on a hypervisor
There is no difference; the words are interchangeable
A VM is always smaller and faster than a container

questions.explanation: A container is an isolated process that shares the host kernel, so it is lightweight. A VM runs a full guest OS on a hypervisor, which is heavier.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes images and containers?

options.text: An image is a running process; a container is a template
An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of that image
Each image can produce exactly one container
Containers are stored in registries; images are not

questions.explanation: An image is a read-only template. A container is a running instance created from an image, with a thin writable layer added on top. One image can produce many containers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are parts of the Docker architecture? Select all that apply.

options.text: A registry such as Docker Hub
A required cloud account that runs your containers remotely

questions.explanation: The client talks to the daemon, which runs containers and pulls or pushes images to a registry. Docker runs locally; no remote cloud account is required.

questions.prompt: Because Docker builds images that follow the ______ standard, they also run on other compliant tools. (three-letter acronym)
questions.explanation: The Open Container Initiative (OCI) standardizes the image and runtime formats, which is what makes images portable across compliant tools.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A read-only template used to create containers
A running, isolated instance of an image
A service that stores and distributes images
The daemon that builds images and runs containers

questions.explanation: The image is the template, a container is a running instance, a registry stores images, and dockerd is the engine doing the work.

questions.prompt: You run `docker run nginx` and the image is not on your machine yet. Order what happens.

items.text: The docker client sends the command to the daemon
The daemon pulls the nginx image from the registry
The daemon creates a container from the image

questions.explanation: The client hands the command to the daemon, which pulls the missing image, creates a container from it, and starts the process.
